study_identification.title: Normative Modeling of Brain Morphometry in Clinical High Risk for Psychosis

study_characteristics.study_objective: Quantify individual-level deviations from normative neuroanatomical variation in CHR-P and evaluate overlap with healthy variation and associations with positive symptoms, cognition, and conversion to psychosis.

clinical_application_and_analysis.association_analysis: - Linear regression (R 4.1.2) relating regional z-scores and ADS to positive symptoms and IQ (age as covariate), with/without site as random effect; 2-proportion z tests for group differences in infra-/supranormal proportions; linear SVC (10-fold CV) for classification; Brain Basis Set (BBS) multivariate modeling.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_brief: Regional deviations largely nested within healthy range; small minority show extreme deviations; higher infranormal ADS in CHR-P; limited associations with symptoms; converters show more infranormal temporal deviations.
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_findings_detailed: Distributions of observed values, regional z-scores, and ADS overlapped between CHR-P and healthy. For any region, CHR-P infranormal/supranormal proportions were low (<11.42% and <7.01%) and similar to healthy (<9.30% and <6.95%). A higher percentage of CHR-P had infranormal global ADS (χ2=12.82, PFDR=6.85e-4), SV ADS (χ2=5.68, PFDR=.02), and SA ADS (χ2=16.01, PFDR=2.53e-4). Within CHR-P, SA ADS associated with positive symptoms (β=-0.08, PFDR=.02; not significant with site random effect) and with IQ (β=0.09, PFDR=.02); global ADS associated with IQ (β=0.10, PFDR=.01). Converters (CHR-PC) had greater infranormal values in right inferior temporal thickness vs healthy (5.10% vs 0.89%) and in right bank of STS surface area vs CHR-PNC (7.01% vs 1.38%). Linear SVC could not classify groups (AUC≈0.47–0.56).
clinical_application_and_analysis.key_limitations: Multi-site data with different scanners/protocols despite harmonization and robustness checks may retain residual site effects; cross-sectional neuroimaging prevents assessment of longitudinal changes.
clinical_application_and_analysis.application_notes: Normative modeling leveraged lifespan CentileBrain models with harmonization and covariate optimization; alternate normative models (GAMLSS; voxelwise GPR) and alternate ADS definitions were explored in Supplement.

general_notes.general_notes: Reference normative models trained on 81 datasets via CentileBrain (MFPR; ComBat-GAM). Full list of datasets not enumerated in article. Sex-specific models; z-scores computed as (Yo-Ŷ)/RMSE.
